pr_title: drivers: ieee802154: cc13xx_cc26xx: add subghz power saving
pr_body:
When stopping the interface, also abort the RX routine and enable RF power saving. Will re-start RX on iface start.

Also fixed a bug with `cmd_fs` crashing at RF wakeup because `rf_mode` was allocated on stack.

Fixes #36695.
pr_comments:
Minor code changes requested, otherwise looks good.

Otherwise, could you please verify

1. that the if can come down and then go back up again (copy-pasted console output with debug statements would be great)
1. that `samples/net/sockets/echo_server` / `samples/net/sockets/echo_client` can run overnight and that few (if any) packets were lost?

Thanks!
Hi, I tested and worked OK, I will get back to you on thursday with some debug logs (I'm a bit away from my devices). Ty.

issue_context.title: net: ieee802154: cc13xx_26xx: Sub-GHz RF power saving
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
I am using the CC13x2 Sub-GHz RF module and I need to turn off the radio on a IEEE802154 interface to save power and be able to enter S2 (standby).
Currently, the API doesn't allow me to do that.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
The easiest way would be to power down the radio when stopping the net interface, then we can call `net_if_down` and `net_if_up` in application code to control usage.

Though when re-starting the interface, other processes (IPv6 DAD and NS) will automatically run again, which is annoying (though I can disable them using config). So I wouldn't mind a network management command for avoiding this.

I implemented the simple solution and will come with a pull request.
I also found a crash bug during wakeup due to `cmd_fs` using a stack-allocated pointer to `rf_mode`.

review_comments: Was it necessary to move this? It would be best to reduce the PR to only the relevant code changes.

Hi, yes it is. Let me explain:
`RF_open()` from TI's library expects the `RF_Mode* pRfMode` parameter with the operation mode & patches to apply to the radio module. Its implementation stores this pointer to an internal structure for lazy usage (the radio will be initialized on first use):
```c
/* Register the mode to the client */
pObj->clientConfig.pRfMode = pRfMode;
````

Actually, the radio is [re]initialized during each power up sequence, including every time after suspend. 
So the catch is... the structure was initialized on stack, which would get replaced once the `ieee802154_cc13xx_cc26xx_subg_init` function returned, so the pointer stored inside RF lib's `clientConfig` would become invalid. So, instead, I allocate it inside DATA section => problem solved.
if `ieee802154_cc13xx_cc26xx_subg_stop()` is no longer used, let's rename this `ieee802154_cc13xx_cc26xx_subg_stop()` and delete the dead code / old implementation.
It is required because `ieee802154_cc13xx_cc26xx_subg_stop` (the old one, without `_if`) only aborts the RX command, which is used through the module as utility function.
